quotes.quote: Because of drop-outs it can happen that some individuals were scanned only at a single time point. Instead of removing this valuable information, it is possible (e.g. in the linear mixed effects models LME) to include this data.

For that it, however, becomes necessary to run the single time points through the longitudinal stream, to ensure that also those images undergo the same processing steps. This can be done by simply passing a single time point in the base creation step.

rows.summary: A dropout with only one scan need not always be excluded: the documentation states such single time-point subjects can be included (e.g., in linear mixed effects models) by running the single time point through the longitudinal stream, passing a single time point in the base creation step. The documentation does not state that cross-sectional output can simply be mixed with longitudinal outputs; rather, it requires the single time point to be processed through the longitudinal stream so the same processing steps apply. The documentation does not state whether other subjects' change estimates should compare against the within-subject template. The documentation scope is historical FreeSurfer documentation (FS 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 6.0), not verified against an installed version.
